{{short description|Belgian astronaut}}
[[File:Photo VP in PF DC9 in 1995.jpg|thumb|275px|Vladimir Pletser in free-float during parabolic flights aboard the NASA DC9/30 in October 1995.]]
'''Vladimir Pletser''' (born 28 February 1956) is Director of Space Training Operations at [[Blue Abyss]] since 2018, where he is in charge of developing astronaut training programs. From 2016 to early 2018, he was a Visiting Professor and Scientific Adviser at the Technology and Engineering Centre for Space Utilization (CSU) of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] in Beijing, China. He supported the preparation of scientific experiments in microgravity for the Chinese [[Tiangong space station]] and for aircraft parabolic flights. He worked previously from 1985 till early 2016 as a senior Physicist Engineer at the [[European Space Research and Technology Centre]] (ESTEC) of [[ESA]].

He is an expert in [[microgravity]] during aircraft [[parabolic flight]]s for which he holds a world record.<ref name="Guinness">{{cite web |title=Most aircraft flown in parabolas by an individual |publisher=Guinness World Records Corporate |url=http://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/records-8000/most-aircraft-flown-in-parabolas-by-an-individual |accessdate=28 January 2012}}</ref> He is known as ‘Mister Parabolic Flights’, ‘Mister Parabolas’,<ref name="MrVolsPar">{{cite news |title=Dans l'antichambre d'un vol spatial |newspaper=Le Soir |location=Brussels |pages=3–7 |language=French |date=18 November 2000 |url=http://archives.lesoir.be/dans-l-antichambre-d-un-vol-spatial-l-impesanteur-pour_t-20001118-Z0JY34.html |accessdate=28 January 2012}}</ref> ‘Homo Parabolicus’<ref name="MrVolsPar"/> or ‘Mister Microgravity’.<ref name="MrMicrogr">{{cite web |title=5000ème parabole pour " Monsieur Microgravité " ! |language=French |publisher=ESA |date=31 March 2008 |url=http://www.esa.int/esaCP/SEM2Q95QGEF_Belgium_fr_0.html |accessdate=28 January 2012}}</ref>

An [[astronaut]] candidate for Belgium since 1991, he spent two months in training in 1995 at NASA's [[Johnson Space Center]] in Houston. Selected by the [[Mars Society]] in 2001, he participated in three international campaigns of crewed Mars mission simulations.

==Early life==
Pletser was born in [[Brussels]], [[Belgium]].

Graduated in Latin-Mathematics from the ''Institut Saint-Boniface'' of Brussels in 1973 and in Special Scientific from the ''Collège Saint-Michel'' of Brussels in 1974; graduated from the ''[[Université Catholique de Louvain]]'' (UCL) in Louvain-la-Neuve, Belgium, as civil engineer in mechanics, specialism dynamics and systems (1979), Master in physics in space geodesy (1980), and Ph.D. in physics in [[astronomy]] and [[astrophysics]] (1990).

==Organisations==
[[International Academy of Astronautics]]; [[International Astronautical Federation]]; [[Committee on Space Research]] (COSPAR); European Low Gravity Research Association; [[European Physical Society]]; [[Belgian Physical Society]]; [[:fr:Société royale belge d'astronomie|Société royale belge d'Astronomie, de Météorologie et de Physique du Globe]]; [[American Mathematical Society]]; Belgian Mathematical Society; [[British Interplanetary Society]]; [[Association of Mars Explorers]]; The [[Mars Society]]; Mars Society Belgium; Euro Space Society; European Interplanetary Free Floaters; The Society of Interplanetary Free Floaters and other scientific and technical organizations.

==Career==
Pletser worked as Research Engineer from 1980 to 1981 at the Department of External Geophysics of the [[Royal Meteorological Institute]] of Belgium on the [[Ionosphere|ionospheric]] [[Doppler effect]], and, from 1981 to 1982, at the Faculty of Agronomy of the [[Université Catholique de Louvain]] on problems of applied [[statistics]], [[mathematical modeling]] and [[computer simulation]]. In 1982, he became assistant professor at the Faculty of Sciences of the [[Université Catholique de Louvain]] and detached at the [[University of Kinshasa]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo|Congo]] (ex-[[Zaire]]), where he lectured until 1985 in Physics, Applied Mathematics, Astronomy and Geophysics.

===Career at ESA===
In 1985, Pletser joined the Microgravity Project and Platform Division in the Human Spaceflight and Operations Directorate at [[ESA]]’s [[ESTEC]] in [[Noordwijk]], [[Netherlands]].

===Development of scientific instrumentation===
Since 1985, he has followed the technical development of scientific payloads and was directly involved in 30 microgravity experiments carried out during space missions as Experiment Coordinator and Responsible for ground operations for experiments:
# in [[fluid physics]] with the Advanced Fluid Physics Module<ref name="AFPM">{{cite journal |last1=Pletser |first1=V. |last2=Gonfalone |first2=A. |last3=Verga |first3=A. |last4=Raimondo |first4=F. |last5=Defilippi |first5=V. |last6=Gily |first6=A. |title=The Advanced Fluid Physics Module: A technical description |journal=Advances in Space Research |volume=11 |issue=7 |pages=101–105 |date=1991 |doi=10.1016/0273-1177(91)90268-O |bibcode=1991AdSpR..11g.101P }}</ref> on Spacelab D2 - [[STS-55]] mission of April 1993, and the Bubble, Drop and Particle Unit<ref name="ESA PL IML2">{{cite journal |last=Walter |first=H.U. |title=ESA's Participation in the International Microgravity Laboratory (IML-2) Mission |journal=ESA Bulletin |volume=81 |publisher=ESA |date=February 1995 |pages=22 |pmid=14971369 |bibcode=1995ESABu..81...22W |url=http://www.esa.int/esapub/bulletin/bullet81/walte81.htm |accessdate=28 January 2012}}</ref><ref name="BDPU-LMS">{{cite journal |last=Pletser |first=V. |title=The Bubble, Drop, Particle Unit on Spacelab LMS, nominal and troubleshooting operations |journal=Acta Astronautica |volume=40 |issue=9 |pages=639–654 |date=May 1997 |bibcode=1997AcAau..40..639P |doi=10.1016/S0094-5765(97)00135-5}}</ref> on Spacelab LMS – [[STS-78]] mission of June 1996.
# in [[protein crystallization]] with the Advanced Protein Crystallization Facility<ref name="ESA PL IML2"/> on Spacehab-[[STS-95]] mission of October 1998, and the Protein Crystallisation Diagnostics Facility<ref name="PCDF">{{cite web |title=Protein Crystallisation Diagnostic Facility (PCDF) |publisher=ESA |date=19 March 2003 |url=http://www.esa.int/esaMI/Columbus/ESAOTN0VMOC_0.html |accessdate=28 January 2012}}<br />{{cite journal |last1=Pletser |first1=V. |last2=Stapelmann |first2=J. |last3=Potthast |first3=L. |last4=Bosch |first4=R. |title=The Protein Crystallization Diagnostics Facility, a new European instrument to investigate biological macromolecular crystal growth on board the International Space Station |journal=Journal of Crystal Growth |volume=196 |issue=2–4 |pages=638–648 |date=1999 |bibcode=1999JCrGr.196..638P |doi=10.1016/S0022-0248(98)00865-3}} <br />{{cite web |title=Protein experiment starts in Columbus laboratory |publisher=ESA |date=27 March 2009 |url=http://www.esa.int/esaMI/Columbus/SEM9ZIKTYRF_0.html |accessdate=28 January 2012}}</ref> (PCDF) that flew aboard the ISS [[Columbus (ISS module)|Columbus]] module ([[STS-122]]) from February 2008 to July 2009 ([[STS-119]]/[[STS-127]]).
# on zeolites with the instruments Zeogrid<ref name="Zeogrid/Nanoslab">{{cite web |title=Study of the structure and morphology of zeogrids obtained under microgravity conditions (ZEOGRID) - Study of aggregation mechanism and kinetics of ZSM-5 and Silicalite-1 nanoslabs into ZSM-5 / Silicalite-1 hybrid phases under microgravity conditions (NANOSLAB) |publisher=ESA |url=http://eea.spaceflight.esa.int/?pg=exprec&id=8007&t=2538583042}}</ref> in the ISS Russian [[Zvezda (ISS module)|Zvezda]] module in October 1992 and Nanoslab<ref name="Zeogrid/Nanoslab"/> in the ISS [[Destiny (ISS module)|Destiny]] module in October 1992 and October 1993.
# on symbiotic processes between fishes and algae with the instrument AquaHab<ref name="InstrESAFotonM3">{{cite web |title=Foton-M3 Mission |publisher=ESA |date=2007 |url=http://esamultimedia.esa.int/docs/foton/FOTON-M3_brochure.pdf |accessdate=28 January 2012}}</ref> aboard the Russian satellite Foton M3 in September 2007.

===Parabolic flights===
From 1985 till early 2016, Pletser was responsible for [[Reduced gravity aircraft|ESA aircraft parabolic flight campaigns]] for short-duration [[microgravity]] experiments.

====ESA Research and Student campaigns====
He organized and led 65 [[:fr:campagnes de vols paraboliques de l’ESA|ESA microgravity research campaigns]] for physical, life sciences, and technology experiments with NASA's [[Reduced gravity aircraft|KC-135/930]] from 1985 to 1988, [[CNES]]’s [[Sud Aviation Caravelle|Caravelle]] from 1989 to 1995, the Russian [[Gagarin Cosmonaut Training Center]]’s [[Ilyushin Il-76]]MDK in 1994, the Dutch [[Royal Netherlands Aerospace Centre|NLR]] [[Cessna Citation II]]<ref name="CessnaCitationII">{{cite web |title=PH-LAB: Cessna Citation II research aircraft |publisher=ESA |date=2007 |url=http://www.nlr.nl/documents/flyers/F108-05.pdf |accessdate=28 January 2012}}</ref> in 2001, the CNES-ESA’s [[Reduced gravity aircraft|Airbus A300 ZERO-G]]<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Pletser |first1=V. |last2=Rouquette |first2=S. |last3=Friedrich |first3=U. |last4=Clervoy |first4=J.F. |last5=Gharib |first5=T. |last6=Gai |first6=F. |last7=Mora |first7=C. |title=European parabolic flight campaigns with Airbus A300 ZERO-G: looking back at the A300 and looking forward to the A310 |journal=Advances in Space Research |volume=56 |issue=5 |pages=1003–1013 |date=2015 |doi=10.1016/j.asr.2015.05.022}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Pletser |first1=V. |last2=Harrod |first2=J. |title=The Science of Gravity; A new era of ESA experiments on parabolic flights |journal=ESA Bulletin |issue=160 |pages=22–33 |date=2014 |url=http://esamultimedia.esa.int/multimedia/publications/ESABulletin160/ |accessdate=25 August 2016}}</ref> from 1997 to 2014, and the [[Airbus A310 |Airbus A310 ZERO-G]]<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Pletser |first1=V. |last2=Rouquette |first2=S. |last3=Friedrich |first3=U. |last4=Clervoy |first4=J.F. |last5=Gharib |first5=T. |last6=Gai |first6=F. |last7=Mora |first7=C. |title=The first European parabolic flight campaigns with the Airbus A310 ZERO-G |journal=Microgravity Science and Technology |volume=28 |issue=6 |pages=587–601 |date=2016 |doi=10.1007/s12217-016-9515-8 |url=http://rdcu.be/jRcH |accessdate=25 August 2016 |bibcode=2016MicST..28..587P|s2cid=255560560 |url-access=subscription }}</ref> since 2015.  In 2011 and 2012, he organized and led with [[CNES]] and [[German Aerospace Center|DLR]] the first two Joint European Partial-g Parabolic Flight campaigns for research at Moon and Mars gravity levels<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Pletser |first1=V. |last2=Winter |first2=J. |last3=Duclos |first3=F. |last4=Friedrich |first4=U. |last5=Clervoy |first5=J.F. |last6=Gharib |first6=T. |last7=Gai |first7=F. |last8=Minster |first8=O. |last9=Sundblad |first9=P. |title=The first Joint European Partial-g Parabolic Flight Campaign at Moon and Mars gravity levels for science and exploration |journal=Microgravity Science and Technology |volume=24 |issue=6 |pages=383–395 |date=2012 |doi=10.1007/s12217-016-9515-8 |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007%2Fs12217-012-9304-y |accessdate=25 August 2016 |bibcode=2016MicST..28..587P|s2cid=255560560 |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Pletser |first1=V. |last2=Rouquette |first2=S. |last3=Friedrich |first3=U. |last4=Clervoy |first4=J.F. |last5=Gharib |first5=T. |last6=Gai |first6=F. |title=Two Joint European Partial-g Parabolic Flight Campaigns for science and exploration at Moon and Mars gravity levels |journal=Paper IAC-13.A2.3.11x19544, Microgravity Sciences and Process Symposium, Session A2 and Space Exploration Symposium, Session A3, 64th IAF Congress, Beijing |date=2013}}</ref> with the Airbus A300 ZERO-G.

From 1994 to 2006, he took part in the organization and the flights of 8 ESA Student campaigns with CNES’s [[Sud Aviation Caravelle|Caravelle]] in 1994, NASA’s [[Reduced gravity aircraft|KC-135/931]] in 1995 and the [[Reduced gravity aircraft|Airbus A300 ZERO-G]] from 2000 to 2006. Since 2010, he participates in ESA's ‘Fly Your Thesis [http://www.esa.int/Education/Fly_Your_Thesis]’ programme,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Callens |first1=N. |last2=Ventura-Traveset |first2=J. |last3=De Lophem |first3=T.L. |last4=Lopez de Echazarreta |first4=C. |last5=Pletser |first5=V. |last6=Van Loon |first6=J. |title=ESA Parabolic Flights, Drop Tower and Centrifuge Opportunities for University Students |journal=Microgravity Science and Technology |volume=23 |issue=2 |pages=181–189 |date=2011 |doi=10.1007/s12217-016-9515-8 |bibcode=2016MicST..28..587P|s2cid=255560560 }}</ref> inviting European University students to submit experiment proposals related to their thesis research. The selected experiments take then part in research campaigns.

====Brussels and Belgium student campaigns====
In 2002, he initiated a new project in Belgium, to have secondary school students flying in weightlessness during ESA Student campaigns. Collaborating with the Region of [[Brussels]]-Capital and the Euro Space Society, he organized a contest for secondary schools in Brussels<ref name="Bxl0g1">{{cite web |title=Bordeaux-Bruxelles-Bordeaux: des élèves belges en chute libre à bord d'un laboratoire volant de l'ESA |language=French |publisher=ESA |date=29 May 2003 |url=http://www.esa.int/esaCP/SEMED2T1VED_Belgium_fr_0.html |accessdate=28 January 2012}}</ref> inviting students to propose experiments to be realized in microgravity. Five teams of Brussels secondary schools<ref name="Bxl0g2">{{cite web |title=Busy weeks ahead for high-flying students |publisher=ESA |date=15 July 2003 |url=http://www.esa.int/esaHS/SEM93GXO4HD_research_0.html |accessdate=28 January 2012}}<br />{{cite web |title=Vingt jeunes d'écoles de Bruxelles à la découverte de la microgravité |language=French |publisher=ESA |date=18 July 2003 |url=http://www.esa.int/esaCP/SEMY0SXO4HD_Belgium_fr_0.html |accessdate=28 January 2012}}<br />{{cite news |title=Expérience " d'enfer " en apesanteur |newspaper=Le Soir |location=Brussels |page=18 |language=French |date=23 July 2003 |url=http://archives.lesoir.be/experience-%3C%3C-d-enfer-%3E%3E-en-apesanteur_t-20030723-Z0NCV0.html |accessdate=28 January 2012}}</ref> took part in the third ESA Student campaign in July 2003 aboard the [[Reduced gravity aircraft|Airbus A300 ZERO-G]] operating for the first time out of [[France]] and landing in [[Brussels]]. This pedagogical project encountered such a large success that it was repeated in 2006 with the [[Belgian Federal Science Policy Office]] and the Euro Space Society for secondary school students of the whole of Belgium.<ref name="Bxl0g4">{{cite web |title=Elèves du secondaire, éprouvez l'effet Zero G! |language=French |publisher=ESA |date=19 September 2005 |url=http://www.esa.int/esaCP/SEMCZT7X9DE_Belgium_fr_0.html |accessdate=28 January 2012}}<br />{{cite web |title=Des élèves de six écoles secondaires vont faire l'expérience de la microgravité |language=French |publisher=ESA |date=20 March 2006 |url=http://www.esa.int/esaCP/SEMJHXNVGJE_Belgium_fr_0.html |accessdate=28 January 2012}}</ref> In July 2006, six teams of Belgian secondary schools participated in the ninth ESA Student campaign with the Airbus A300 landing again in [[Brussels]].

====Participation in other campaigns====
Pletser was invited to participate in several other campaigns. In 1992, he participated in a [[German Aerospace Center|DLR]] campaign aboard NASA's [[Reduced gravity aircraft|KC-135/930]] in Houston to train German astronauts on AFPM<ref name="AFPM"/> operations prior to the Spacelab D2 - [[STS-55]] mission. In 1993, he participated in parabolic flights aboard a [[Fouga Magister]] of the [[Belgian Air Component|Belgian Air Force]] to measure [[microgravity]] levels during flights. In 1995, he was invited by [[NASA]] to participate in a campaign aboard the [[McDonnell Douglas DC-9|DC-9/30]] of the [[Glenn Research Center|Lewis Research Center]] to prepare a BDPU<ref name="BDPU-LMS"/> experiment for the Spacelab LMS - [[STS-78]] mission. In 1999, he was invited to participate in two campaigns of the [[CNES]] and the [[German Aerospace Center|DLR]] with the [[Reduced gravity aircraft|Airbus A300 ZERO-G]] as subject of a medical experiment. In 2004, he was invited to fly aboard the Austrian Short Skyvan aircraft.<ref name="ShortSkyvan">{{cite web |title=Paul's parabelflüge |language=German |date=9 July 2004 |url=http://www.bierl.at/parabelflug/newsframeset.htm |accessdate=28 January 2012}}</ref> In 2011, the [[Canadian Space Agency]] invited him to participate in a series of parabolic flights aboard the [[Dassault Falcon 20|Falcon 20]] in [[Ottawa]] to support a [[combustion]] experiment. In 2016, he participated as a visiting professor in the Space Studies Programme (SSP-16) of the [[International Space University]] (ISU) taking place at the [[Technion]] in [[Haifa]], [[Israël]]. He takes part in a series of parabolic flights on board a [[Grob G103a Twin II]] glider organized by ISU's Space Sciences Department, performing several experiments proposed by ISU students, conducting therefore the first scientific parabolic flights in the Middle East.

====Number of experiments and parabolas====
During the 90 campaigns in which he took part, he supervised a total of 1000 [[microgravity]] experiments. He was Principal Investigator of 11 experiments of micro-[[Accelerometer|accelerometric]] measurement of [[microgravity]] levels and of 2 fluid physics experiments. He participated as operator in 79 physical science experiments and as subject in 95 medical and physiological experiments in preparation for several missions on [[Spacelab]], [[Spacehab]], the Russian space station [[Mir]], and the [[International Space Station]]. He accumulated 7389 parabolas, totaling 39h 34m in weightlessness, equivalent to 26.3 [[Geocentric orbit|Earth orbits]], more than the first American, the first Russian, or the first Chinese astronauts. He accumulated a total of 53m in Martian gravity and 50m in lunar gravity during partial-g parabolic flights.

====World record for the number of aircraft in parabolic flight====
Pletser is the only person in the world having flown parabolas on 14 different aircraft: NASA's [[Reduced gravity aircraft|KC-135/930]], [[Reduced gravity aircraft|KC-135/931]], and [[McDonnell Douglas DC-9|DC-9/30]]; the [[ESA]]–[[CNES]]–[[German Aerospace Center|DLR]]’s [[Airbus A310]] ZERO-G; the [[CNES]]-[[ESA]]’s [[Reduced gravity aircraft|Airbus A300 ZERO-G]]; the [[CNES]]’s [[Sud Aviation Caravelle|Caravelle]]; the Russian [[Gagarin Cosmonaut Training Center]] [[Ilyushin Il-76]]MDK; the [[Canadian Space Agency]]’s [[Dassault Falcon 20|Falcon 20]]; the Dutch [[Royal Netherlands Aerospace Centre|NLR]] [[Cessna Citation II]];<ref name="CessnaCitationII"/> a [[Fouga Magister]] of the [[Belgian Air Component|Belgian Air Force]]; the Austrian [[Short Skyvan]];<ref name="ShortSkyvan"/> a [[Grob G103a Twin II]] glider; an [[ASK21]] glider; and a [[Cessna 150]]. He holds the official Guinness World Record<ref name="Guinness"/> for the most aircraft flown in parabolic flight (nine), awarded in 2010 before his participation in the flights aboard the [[Dassault Falcon 20|Falcon 20]] in 2011, the [[Airbus A310]] since 2015, the [[Grob G103a Twin II]] glider in 2016, and the [[ASK21]] glider in 2018.

==Mars Crewed Mission Simulation campaigns==
[[File:Vladimir Pletser in Martian EVA suit.jpg|thumb|Vladimir Pletser in Martian Extra-vehicular suit at the [[FMARS]]]]

In 2001, Pletser was selected<ref name="FMARS1">{{cite journal |last=Pletser |first=V. |title=Simulation of a manned Martian mission in the Arctic Circle |journal=ESA Bulletin |volume=108 |pages=121–123 |publisher=ESA |date=November 2001 |url=http://www.esa.int/esapub/bulletin/bullet108/chapter15_bul108.pdf |accessdate=28 January 2012}}<br />{{cite web |title=Mars Society Flashline Volunteers Selected for 2001 Field Season |publisher=SpaceRef |date=15 March 2001 |url=http://www.spaceref.com/news/viewpr.html?pid=4124 |accessdate=28 January 2012}}<br />{{cite news |title=Un Belge "sur Mars" |newspaper=Le Soir |location=Brussels |pages=7 |language=French |date=9 April 2001 |url=http://archives.lesoir.be/espace2001-mars-odyssey-l-aventure-recommence-la-conque_t-20010409-Z0KAPZ.html |accessdate=28 January 2012}}<br />{{cite news |title=Un Belge sur Mars pendant dix jours Le docteur Pletser séjourne dans un module martien... posé en Arctique |newspaper=Le Soir |location=Brussels |pages=7 |language=French |date=2 July 2001 |url=http://archives.lesoir.be/espace-un-belge-sur-mars-pendant-dix-jours-le-docteur-p_t-20010712-Z0KP93.html |accessdate=28 January 2012}}<br />{{cite news |title=Mission martienne pour un Belge |newspaper=La Dernière Heure |location=Brussels |pages=14 |language=French |date=29 June 2001 |url=http://www.dhnet.be/dhjournal/archives_det.phtml?id=39381 |accessdate=28 January 2012}}</ref> by the [[Mars Society]] among 250 candidates to participate in July 2001 in the first international Mars crewed mission simulation campaign at the [[Flashline Mars Arctic Research Station]] (FMARS) on the [[Devon Island]] in the [[Canadian Arctic Archipelago|Canadian Arctic]] with the FMARS-2 crew. He conducted an experiment aiming at detecting subsurface water by a seismic method.<ref name="FMARS4">{{cite journal |last1=Pletser |first1=V. |last2=Lognonne |first2=P. |last3=Diament |first3=M. |last4=Dehant |first4=V. |title=Subsurface water detection on Mars by astronauts using a seismic refraction method: Tests during a manned Mars mission simulation |journal=Acta Astronautica |volume=64 |issue=4 |pages=457–466 |date=February 2009 |bibcode=2009AcAau..64..457P |doi=10.1016/j.actaastro.2008.07.005}}<br />{{cite news |title=Sale temps pour l'équipage martien posé dans le Grand Nord canadien |newspaper=Le Soir |location=Brussels |pages=7 |language=French |date=19 July 2001 |url=http://archives.lesoir.be/sale-temps-pour-l-equipage-martien-pose-dans-le-grand_t-20010719-Z0KQ1E.html |accessdate=28 January 2012}}</ref> Invited again by The [[Mars Society]], he participated in April 2002 in a second international crewed Mars mission simulation campaign<ref name="MDRS1">{{cite news |last=Real |first=D. |title=Mission to... Utah? |newspaper=The Dallas Morning News |location=Dallas, Texas |publisher=Dallas News |date=6 July 2002 |url=http://homepage.mac.com/WJClancey/~WJClancey/RealStory02.html |accessdate=28 January 2012}} <br />{{cite news |last=Laurence |first=C. |title=Life on Mars |newspaper=The Telegraph |publisher=Telegraph Media Group Limited |date=5 May 2002 |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/science/science-news/4768432/Life-on-Mars.html |accessdate=28 January 2012}} <br />{{cite news |title=Objectif Mars : Un astronaute belge en isolement total dans le désert de l'Utah |newspaper=La Dernière Heure |location=Brussels |pages=14 |language=French |date=8 April 2002 |url=http://www.dhnet.be/infos/societe/article/37529/objectif-mars.html |accessdate=28 January 2012}}</ref> in the [[Mars Desert Research Station]] (MDRS) in the [[Utah]] Desert with the crew MDRS-5 in strict isolation for two weeks. He was responsible for a psychological experiment on growing plants in the Mars habitat.<ref name="PsychPlantGro">{{Citation |last1=Pletser |first1=V. |last2=Lasseur |first2=C. |contribution=First observation regarding the psychological impact of growing vegetables during a manned Mars mission simulation at the Mars Desert Research Station |title=First observation regarding the psychological impact of growing vegetables during a manned Mars mission simulation at the Mars Desert Research Station |series=Proceedings 54th International Astronautical Federation Congress, Paper IAC-03-IAA.10.3.04 |publisher=International Astronautical Federation |date=October 2003 |contribution-url=http://www.zarm.uni-bremen.de/iaf2003/abstracts/data/pdf/IAC-03-IAA.10.3.04.PDF}}</ref> During these two missions, he kept a diary at the FMARS<ref name="ESAwebFMARS">{{cite web |title=En route for 'Mars' |publisher=ESA |date=29 September 2004 |url=http://www.esa.int/esaCP/ESAB000VMOC_Life_0.html |accessdate=28 January 2012}}</ref> and at the MDRS.<ref name="MDRS2">{{cite web |title=Postcard from Mars 2 |publisher=ESA |date=8 April 2002 |url=http://www.esa.int/esaHS/ESALDSF18ZC_exploration_0.html |accessdate=28 January 2012}}</ref> He published a book<ref>{{cite book |last=Pletser |first=V. |title=En avant, Mars ! Chroniques de simulations martiennes |publisher=Labor |date=2003 |page=197 |language=French |isbn=978-2-8040-1773-6}} <br />{{cite web |title=En avant, Mars ! |language=French |publisher=Labrot |date=30 June 2002 |url=http://www.nirgal.net/critiques/en_avant_mars.html |accessdate=28 January 2012}}</ref> about these two simulations. In 2009, in the frame of ESA's EuroGeoMars project<ref name="EuroGeoMars1">{{Citation |last1=Foing |first1=B.H. |last2=Boche-Sauvan |first2=L. |last3=Stoker |first3=C. |last4=Ehrenfreund |first4=P. |last5=Wendt |first5=L. |last6=Gross |first6=C. |last7=Thiel |first7=C. |last8=Peters |first8=S. |last9=Borst |first9=A. | last10 = Zhavaleta| first10 = J. |last11=Sarrazin |first11=P. |last12=Blake |first12=D. |last13=Page |first13=J. |last14=Pletser |first14=V. |last15=Monaghan |first15=E. |contribution=ExoHab & EuroGeoMars campaigns: Human exploration and astrobiology |title=ExoHab & EuroGeoMars campaigns: Human exploration and astrobiology |series=Proceedings Astrobiology Science Conference: Evolution and Life: Surviving Catastrophes and Extremes on Earth and Beyond, Paper 5625 |date=2010 |url=http://www.lpi.usra.edu/meetings/abscicon2010/pdf/5625.pdf}}</ref> to study human and scientific aspects of future crewed missions on extra-planetary surfaces, he participated in a third Martian simulation campaign at the MDRS as Crew Commander of Crew MDRS-76. He was responsible for a series of experiments on human crew aspects.<ref name="CrewAspects1">{{cite journal |last1=Pletser |first1=V. |last2=Foing |first2=B.H. |title=European Contribution to Human Aspect Investigations for Future Planetary Habitat Definition Studies: Field Tests at MDRS on Crew Time Utilisation and Habitat Interfaces |journal=Microgravity Science and Technology |volume=23 |issue=2 |pages=199–214 |date=2011 |doi=10.1007/s12217-010-9251-4 |bibcode=2011MicST..23..199P|s2cid=122357805 }}</ref> During these three campaigns, he participated in a total of 36 experiments in geophysics, biology, navigation and reconnaissance, psychology and human factors. He accumulated a total of 44h 30m of simulated [[Extra-vehicular activity]] (EVA) time during 16 simulated EVA expeditions, including 9 as Commander.

==ESA and NASA astronaut selections==
Pletser was selected in May 1991 by Belgium among 550 candidates as laboratory specialist astronaut candidate,<ref name="selection1">{{cite news |title=Cinq Belges prêts à partir à la conquête de l'espace. Vladimir Pletser peut officiellement rêver d'Hermes. Vivre le syndrome… |newspaper=Le Soir |location=Brussels |pages=1, 17 |language=French |date=3 May 1991 |url=http://archives.lesoir.be/cinq-belges-prets-a-partir-a-la-conquete-de-l-espace_t-19910503-Z03XJE.html |accessdate=28 January 2012}} <br />{{cite news |title=La route linguistique vers les étoiles : trois francophones sur nos cinq candidats astronautes |newspaper=Le Soir |location=Brussels |page=17 |language=French |date=2 May 1991 |url=http://archives.lesoir.be/la-route-linguistique-vers-les-etoiles-trois_t-19910502-Z03XDE.html |accessdate=28 January 2012}} <br />{{cite web |title=Spacefacts biography of Vladimir Pletser |publisher=Spacefacts |date=30 October 2008 |url=http://www.spacefacts.de/bios/candidates/english/pletser_vladimir.htm |accessdate=28 January 2012}}<br />{{cite journal |title=ESA Astronaut Selections |journal=ESA Bulletin |volume=135 |pages=69–70 |publisher=ESA |date=August 2008 |url=http://www.esa.int/esapub/bulletin/bulletin135/bul135_inbrief.pdf |accessdate=28 January 2012}}</ref> with four other candidates, including [[Marianne Merchez]] and [[Frank De Winne]], but he was not retained at the end of the ESA selection in May 1992. In May 1992, he applied to NASA as [[Payload Specialist]] astronaut candidate for the 2nd International Microgravity Laboratory (IML-2) [[Spacelab]] - [[STS-65]] mission. Although recommended by members of the IML-2 Mission Investigator Working Group, his application was not considered by [[NASA]]. In January 1995, he was officially presented<ref name="SelLMS">{{cite news |title=Un deuxième astronaute belge ? |newspaper=Le Soir |location=Brussels |page=27 |language=French |date=25 March 1995 |url=http://archives.lesoir.be/Un-deuxième-astronaute-belge-_t-19950325-Z099ZG.html |accessdate=28 January 2012}}</ref> by [[Belgium]] as a [[Payload Specialist]] astronaut candidate for [[NASA]]’s Life and Microgravity Spacelab (LMS) - [[STS-78]] mission. Four other candidates were presented respectively by the French Space Agency ([[CNES]]), the [[Canadian Space Agency]] (CSA), the [[Italian Space Agency]] (ASI) and [[ESA]]. After recommendation of the LMS Mission Investigator Working Group, the five candidates reported in March 1995 to NASA's [[Johnson Space Center]] for medical examinations and information sessions on medical experiments. Pletser passed successfully the medical selection and was unofficially informed that one of the places as alternate [[Payload Specialist]] astronaut would be proposed to him, having received the most recommendations of the LMS Mission Investigator Working Group. He started with the three other selected candidates two months of training at NASA's Johnson Space Center, at the Payload Crew Training Complex of NASA's [[Marshall Space Flight Center]] in Huntsville, at [[ESTEC]] and in several American university laboratories. However, NASA announced in May 1995 the selection of Dr. [[Jean-Jacques Favier]] ([[CNES]]) and Dr. [[Robert Thirsk]] ([[Canadian Space Agency|CSA]]) as [[Payload Specialist]] astronauts, and Dr [[Luca Urbani]] ([[Italian Space Agency|ASI]]) and Mr. [[Pedro Duque]] (ESA) as alternate Payload Specialist astronauts.

==Academic and scientific career==
[[File:Vladimir Pletser in SSF 2026.jpg|thumb|Vladimir Pletser in 2026]]
Pletser is visiting professor at several universities in Europe, Africa, Asia, and America. He has given several hundreds of conferences, seminars, and invited lectures in [[microgravity]] research, [[astronautics]], [[astronomy]], [[geophysics]], [[Mars]] exploration, and [[SETI]] in thirty universities and academies and for schools and the general public in Europe, Africa and Asia. As part of the awareness program for youth scientific and technical education and careers<ref name="AmbSci"/> of the Government of the [[Brussels]]-Capital Region, 16,000 school students of Brussels attended his conferences between 2001 and 2011. His theoretical research on the [[cosmogony]] of the [[Solar System]] led to the publication in 1990 of a doctoral thesis<ref name="TheseDoc">{{cite journal |last=Pletser |first=V. |title=On exponential distance relations in planetary and satellite systems, observations and origin |journal=Doctoral Dissertation, Institute of Astronomy and Geophysics G. Lemaître, Dept of Physics, Faculty of Sciences, Université Catholique de Louvain |pages=164 |date=1990}}</ref> on distance relations among [[planets]] and [[satellites]], where the radial positions of the new satellites and [[Planetary ring|ring]]s of [[Uranus]] and [[Neptune]] are calculated before their discovery by the ''[[Voyager 2]]'' probe.<ref name="PapRelExpDist">{{cite journal |last=Pletser |first=V. |title=Lois exponentielles de distance pour les systèmes de satellites |journal=Earth, Moon, and Planets |volume=36 |issue=3 |pages=193–210 |date=1986 |language=French |doi=10.1007/bf00055159 |bibcode=1986EM&P...36..193P|s2cid=120077862 }}<br />{{cite journal |last=Pletser |first=V. |title=Revised exponential distance relation for the Uranian system after the Voyager 2 fly-by |journal=Earth, Moon, and Planets |volume=41 |issue=3 |pages=295–300 |date=1988 |bibcode=1988EM&P...41..295P |doi=10.1007/BF00113991|s2cid=120449402 }}<br />{{cite journal |last=Pletser |first=V. |title=Notes on an initial satellite system of Neptune |journal=Earth, Moon, and Planets |volume=46 |issue=3 |pages=285–295 |date=1989 |doi=10.1007/bf00117195 |bibcode=1989EM&P...46..285P|s2cid=122936979 }}</ref> In 1998, he demonstrated the hypothesis that the [[Ishango bone]], the oldest mathematical tool of humankind, is a primitive calculator in bases 6 and 12.<ref name="OsIshango">{{cite journal |last=Pletser |first=V. |author2=Huylebrouck D. |title=The Ishango Artifact: the Missing Base 12 Link |journal=Forma |volume=14 |issue=4 |pages=339–346 |date=1999 |url=http://www.scipress.org/journals/forma/pdf/1404/14040339.pdf |accessdate=28 January 2012}}</ref> Having been subject of an [[Electroencephalography|electroencephalographic]] experiment in parabolic flights in 1991, he took part in the result analysis and proposed a new method based on the [[Chaos theory|chaotic nonlinear dynamics]],<ref name="PapEEG">{{cite journal |last=Pletser |first=V. |author2=Quadens O. |title=Degraded EEG response of the human brain in function of gravity levels by the method of chaotic attractor |journal=Acta Astronautica |volume=52 |issue=7 |pages=581–589 |date=2003 |doi=10.1016/S0094-5765(02)00124-8 |pmid=12575723 |bibcode=2003AcAau..52..581P}}</ref> yielding in 1999 to the awarding of a patent.<ref name="PatentEEG">{{cite patent |inventor-last=Pletser |inventor-first=V. |inventor2-last=Quadens |inventor2-first=O. |pubdate=2003-12-02 |title=Method and device for the predictive determination of a parameter representative of the mental activity of a person |country=US |number=6658369}}</ref> He is pursuing research in Number Theory, on Generalised Mersenne numbers, on sums of powers of consecutive integers,<ref name="Euler Taxi-Cab">{{cite journal |last=Pletser |first=V. |title= Euler's and the Taxi-Cab relations and other numbers that can be written twice as sums of two cubed integers |journal= Open Journal of Mathematical Sciences |volume= |issue= |pages=|date=2023 |url= https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.00465|accessdate=7 November 2023}}</ref><ref name="Sums of cubes">{{cite journal |last=Pletser |first=V. |title= General solutions of sums of consecutive cubed integers equal to squared integers |journal= Journal of Number Theory |volume=156 |issue= |pages=394–413|date=2015 |url= https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022314X15001699?ref=pdf_download&fr=RR-2&rr=8222513d1ad75bf0|accessdate=7 November 2023}}</ref> on multiple of triangular numbers,<ref name="Multiple Triangular Numbers 1">{{cite journal |last=Pletser |first=V. |title= Recurrent Relations for Triangular Numbers Multiples of Other Triangular Numbers |journal= Indian Journal of Pure and Applied Mathematics |volume=53 |issue=3 |pages=782–791 |date=2022 |url= https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s13226-021-00172-y |accessdate=7 November 2023}}</ref><ref name="Multiple Triangular Numbers 2">{{cite journal |last=Pletser |first=V. |title= Congruence Properties of Indices of Triangular Numbers Multiple of Other Triangular Numbers |journal= Open Journal of Mathematical Sciences |volume=5 |issue=1 |pages=262–269|date=2021 |url=https://pisrt.org/psr-press/journals/oms-vol-5-2021/congruence-properties-of-indices-of-triangular-numbers-multiple-of-other-triangular-numbers/ |accessdate=7 November 2023}}</ref> on characteristics of Pell's equation solutions.<ref name="Continued fractions">{{cite journal |last=Pletser |first=V. |title= On continued fraction development of quadratic irrationals having all periodic terms but last equal and associated general solutions of the Pell equation |journal= Journal of Number Theory |volume=136 |issue= |pages=339–353|date=2013 |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022314X13002771 |accessdate=7 November 2023}}</ref> He is a regular contributor to the [[On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences]].
